about.cta_description: Have questions about SanaGo? We'd love to hear from you and discuss how we can support your healthcare facility.
about.hero_subtitle: We help healthcare providers deliver better care through intuitive, reliable management tools.
about.story_p1: SanaGo was born from a simple observation: most hospital management software is either outdated, overly complex, or prohibitively expensive. Small and medium-sized clinics are left choosing between spreadsheets and enterprise systems they don't need.
about.story_p2: We set out to change that. SanaGo combines deep understanding of clinical workflows with modern, user-friendly design. The result is a hospital management system that's fast, intuitive, and scales from a single clinic to a network of hospitals.
about.story_title: Built for healthcare, designed for people
about.values_accessible_description: Modern web-based interface works on any device. No installations, no plugins — just open your browser and get to work.
about.values_clinician_description: Built with input from doctors, nurses, and hospital administrators. SanaGo solves real clinical workflow challenges, not imagined ones.
about.values_patient_description: Every feature is designed around the patient journey. From registration to discharge, we prioritize efficient, compassionate care delivery.
about.values_security_description: Granular access controls, complete audit logging, and data isolation ensure your hospital data stays protected and compliant at all times.
about.values_subtitle: Our values guide every feature we build and every decision we make.

features.cta_description: See how SanaGo can transform your hospital operations with a personalized demonstration.

features.roles_subtitle: Tailored dashboards ensure each team member sees exactly what they need — nothing more, nothing less.

market.claims_body: Patient insurance, policy numbers and claim lines are part of the record, not a spreadsheet beside it.
market.label: Local detail

inside.c2_body: Vitals, notes and the next appointment in one sitting.

about.proof_body: Two screens a hospital opens on its first Monday: the patient directory and the cashier shift. Both are drawn from the same interface the hospital actually operates.
about.proof_c1: Patient directory · search by name, phone or UID
about.proof_c2: Caisse · one shift, one counted drawer

p1.title: The record is the product
p1.body: Every screen either writes to the patient file or reads from it. When a feature cannot justify itself that way, it does not ship — that rule is why the ward and the cashier agree.

p2.title: Permission, not trust
p2.body: Access is granted per role and per action, and every privileged change is logged with the person, the address and the payload. A hospital should be able to prove who saw what.

p3.title: One hospital, one database
p3.body: Each hospital runs on its own database on its own subdomain. A login from one hospital cannot reach another’s records, however the URL is typed.

p4.title: Built for the shift, not the demo
p4.body: Slow connections, shared terminals, a nurse with gloves on. The interfaces are designed to be operated at speed, in French or English, with the numbers we actually bill in.

promise1.title: A named person on support
promise1.body: Write or call the same team that sets the hospital up — not a queue that reroutes to a reseller.
promise1.body_plain: The team that sets the hospital up is the team that answers when something breaks.

promise2.title: Migration, not a re-typing
promise2.body: Patient lists, tariffs, drug catalogues, staff accounts and wards are loaded before go-live, from the exports your current system already produces.

promise3.title: You keep the data
promise3.body: A full export of the hospital’s records is available at any time, including after a subscription ends. Leaving is a process, not a hostage negotiation.

about.lede: SanaGo exists because small and mid-sized hospitals are offered two bad options: spreadsheets held together by one person, or an enterprise suite priced for a ministry. We build the third one.
about.photo_note: Photography from hospital settings. Unsplash licence.
about.story_title: The gap is not software. It is software priced for this hospital.
about.story_p1: Most hospital software is sold per bed, per module, per year, in a currency the hospital does not earn in. So the work migrates: the patient register becomes a notebook, the pharmacy ledger becomes a spreadsheet, and the cashier reconciles three sources by hand at midnight.
about.story_p2: SanaGo is built the other way around. One hospital, one database, one price in FCFA, and a workflow that assumes the reality of a busy Cameroonian hospital — several stations, shared terminals, patients who arrive without a file, and insurers who pay late.
about.story_p3: The product is deliberately narrow. It does clinical records, diagnostics, stock, wards and money, and it does nothing else until those are excellent.
about.principles_note: Four rules the product is held to.
about.how_note: From signature to the first ward round on the system.
about.how_title: A fortnight to live, not a quarter
about.how1_body: Two weeks from signed agreement to a live subdomain, with the hospital’s own tariffs loaded.
about.how2_body: Per-desk sessions — front office, nursing, laboratory, pharmacy, cashier — in French or English.
about.how3_body: Weekday support by phone and email, with an audit trail of every ticket.
about.how4_body: A quarterly look at what the wards actually use, and what we should stop building.
about.cta_body: Bring your hardest workflow — a transfer between wards, a half-paid invoice, a lab result that changes the treatment. We will walk it on a real screen.

step1.title: You send the form
step1.body: It lands in the platform’s request queue with the hospital name and what you are trying to fix.

step2.title: We reply within a working day
step2.body: A short call to understand the wards, the tariffs and who currently holds the data.

step3.title: A working session, not a slideshow
step3.body: We open the product and walk the workflow you described — with your units and drug names on screen.

contact.lede: The useful demo is the one where you describe the mess and we show you the screen. Send the form, or write straight to the support address — both are read by the same people.

pricing.default_description: A complete hospital workspace for this tier.

patients.title: Patient records
patients.body: One file per patient, opened at the front desk and never re-typed: photo, guardian, blood group, allergies, insurer and the full visit history behind a single search box.

appointments.title: Appointments & queue
appointments.body: Book by desk, doctor or station. The hall list shows who is waiting, who is in consultation and who has not arrived.

consultations.title: Consultations
consultations.body: Structured clinical notes — presenting complaint, examination by system, diagnosis, treatment plan and follow-up — attached to the visit.

admissions.title: Admissions & wards
admissions.body: Admit, transfer a bed, discharge with a summary. Occupancy is live, so the ward knows what is free before the patient arrives.

vitals.title: Vitals & nursing
vitals.body: Temperature, blood pressure, pulse, oxygen saturation, respiration and weight, with abnormal readings flagged at the moment of entry.

laboratory.title: Laboratory
laboratory.body: Requests, specimens and results entered against the test definition, then validated and released to the doctor who ordered them.

radiology.title: Radiology & imaging
radiology.body: Orders by modality — X-ray, ultrasound, CT, MRI — with findings, a conclusion and a signed report archive.

pharmacy.title: Pharmacy & dispensing
pharmacy.body: Dispense against the prescription, batch by batch, with expiry and low-stock warnings before the shelf is empty.

inventory.title: Inventory & supplies
inventory.body: Non-drug stock — consumables, PPE, IV fluids, wound care — with reorder thresholds, usage and current inventory value.

surgery.title: Surgery
surgery.body: Theatre schedule with surgeon, anaesthetist, procedure, fee and complications recorded against the patient.

emergency.title: Emergency
emergency.body: Register an arrival with triage level, arrival mode, assessment and disposition — before a full file exists.

billing.title: Billing & invoicing
billing.body: Invoices with tariff lines, per-doctor pricing, partial payments and the balance carried on the episode.

cash_register.title: Cashier (Caisse)
cash_register.body: Open a shift, take payments, close and reconcile against a counted drawer. Each shift keeps its own ledger.

claims.title: Insurance & tiers payant
claims.body: Patient policies, beneficiaries and insurer claims with the supporting lines the payer will ask for.

certificates.title: Medical certificates
certificates.body: Sick leave, fitness and death certificates issued from the record, numbered and printable.

reports.title: Reports & analytics
reports.body: Revenue by period and service, activity across desks, and the figures the board asks for — without a spreadsheet export.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.body: Who opened, changed or exported a record, and when. Visible to the administrator, not to everyone.

sms.title: SMS notifications
sms.body: Appointment reminders and result notices over MTN and Orange numbers, with email as the fallback channel.

api.title: API access
api.body: Machine-to-machine access for a billing system, an analyser or a national reporting feed.

branding.title: Custom branding
branding.body: The hospital’s own name, mark and subdomain, instead of a generic tenant address.

features.rooms_body: A theatre list, a ward round and a dispensary shelf: three places a hospital loses hours every week, and three places SanaGo is designed to give them back.

matrix.body: Core clinical work is in every tier. Diagnostics, theatre and the money desk are where the tiers separate.

register.title: Register
register.body: A patient file is opened once — photo, guardian, blood group, insurer — and every later visit attaches to it.

triage.title: Triage & queue
triage.body: Vitals at the door, a position in the queue per station, and a waiting list the front desk can see.

consult.title: Consult
consult.body: Structured notes, diagnosis, prescription and the next appointment, written into the same record.

diagnose.title: Diagnostics
diagnose.body: Lab and imaging requests leave the consultation already attached to the patient and the doctor who ordered them.

ward.title: Dispense & admit
ward.body: Pharmacy deducts the batch it dispensed; the ward assigns a real bed and the deposit lands on the account.

settle.title: Bill & settle
settle.body: One invoice per episode, a cash shift that reconciles, and an insurer claim with its supporting lines.

footer.facts_note: Plans, contacts and counts on this site are read live from the platform console.

admin.label: Administration
admin.scope: Users, roles and the whole ledger
admin.a1: Create a role and decide exactly which desks reach which record
admin.a2: Read the audit trail: who opened, edited or exported a file
admin.a3: Watch revenue, stock value and occupancy on one board

doctor.label: Doctor
doctor.scope: Today's list, the record, the prescription pad
doctor.a1: Open any patient with their full history already loaded
doctor.a2: Prescribe against real stock, with allergy warnings inline
doctor.a3: Order labs and imaging without leaving the consultation

nurse.label: Nursing
nurse.scope: Ward rounds, vitals and care reports
nurse.a1: Record vitals in seconds and flag the abnormal ones
nurse.a2: Chart a bed for the night and hand over the shift in writing
nurse.a3: See which prescriptions are still waiting at the pharmacy

lab.label: Laboratory
lab.a1: A worklist of every open request, oldest first
lab.a2: Enter results against the test definition, not free text
lab.a3: Validate and release — the doctor is notified immediately

pharmacy.label: Pharmacy
pharmacy.a1: Dispense from the prescription, batch by batch
pharmacy.a2: Watch expiries and low stock before they become a shortage
pharmacy.a3: Bill the medicines into the same invoice as the consultation

radiology.label: Imaging
radiology.a1: Queue X-ray, ultrasound, CT and MRI orders by modality
radiology.a2: Write findings and a conclusion, then sign the study off
radiology.a3: Keep every report in one searchable archive

cashier.label: Caisse
cashier.a1: Take a payment against the invoice, in cash or by transfer
cashier.a2: Open and close a shift with a counted drawer
cashier.a3: Prepare the insurer claim with its supporting lines

trial.a: Every new hospital starts on a full working trial — no card, no sales call. When it ends the hospital keeps its data and can move onto any plan; nothing is deleted.

patient_cap.q: What happens when we reach the patient limit?
patient_cap.a: The console warns you as you approach the tier ceiling. Nothing breaks and no record is hidden, but new registrations pause until you move up a tier.

upgrade.a: Yes — up or down, at any point. The change is recorded on the subscription with its own invoice, so the finance desk always has an audit trail.

data.q: Where does our patient data live?
data.a: Each hospital gets its own database. Staff on one subdomain cannot reach another hospital’s records even with a valid login, and every privileged action is written to an audit log.

offline.q: Our power and internet are not reliable. Is that a problem?
offline.a: The desk keeps working through short outages and rejoins cleanly. Work that must not be lost — dispensing, payments — is committed to the record, not held in the browser.

payment.a: Invoices are raised in FCFA and settled by transfer or mobile money. An annual plan bills once and costs less than twelve monthly payments.

cta.title: Put the whole hospital on one record.
cta.body: Book a working session and we will show you the desks you care about — with your own units, tariffs and ward names in the room.

agreement.title: The agreement
agreement.p1: These terms govern the use of the SanaGo platform by a hospital, clinic or health centre (the customer) and the people it invites into its workspace. By provisioning a hospital or using a trial, the customer accepts them.

trial.title: Trials
trial.p1: A new hospital starts on a working trial that runs for the number of days published on the pricing page at the time of signup. No payment method is required to start. At the end of the trial the workspace keeps its data and moves to read-only until a plan is taken or the hospital asks for deletion.

plans.title: Plans, quotas and billing
plans.b1: Plans are priced per hospital in the currency shown on the pricing page, billed monthly or annually.
plans.b2: Each plan carries a user limit, a patient-record limit, a storage allowance and a set of unlocked modules. Limits are shown before a plan is chosen.
plans.b3: When a limit is reached, new records in that category pause. Existing records are never hidden or deleted.
plans.b4: Changing plan mid-cycle raises a new invoice for the difference; the change is recorded on the subscription.
plans.b5: After expiry there is a grace period before the workspace becomes read-only. Data is preserved during it.

customer.title: What the hospital is responsible for
customer.b1: Issuing, changing and revoking its own staff accounts, and keeping their roles accurate.
customer.b2: Clinical decisions. SanaGo records and routes information; it does not diagnose, prescribe or replace clinical judgement.
customer.b3: Obtaining any patient consent required by local law for the collection and use of health data.
customer.b4: The accuracy of tariffs, drug catalogues and insurance details entered into the workspace.

data.title: Ownership of data
data.p1: The hospital owns its data. We store and process it to run the service and for support, and we do not sell it or use it to train models. A full export is available on request, including after the subscription ends.

service.title: Availability and support
service.p1: We aim to keep the platform available continuously and to give notice of planned maintenance. Support is provided on working days through the channels published on the contact page; response times depend on the plan.

acceptable.title: Acceptable use
acceptable.b1: No attempts to reach another hospital’s data, to bypass role permissions, or to probe the platform for vulnerabilities without written agreement.
acceptable.b2: No resale, sublicensing or white-labelling of the platform outside the branding options a plan includes.
acceptable.b3: No use of the platform to store records the hospital is not entitled to hold.

suspension.title: Suspension and termination
suspension.p1: A workspace may be suspended for non-payment after the grace period, or immediately where continued operation would be unlawful or would put other hospitals at risk. Where a workspace is suspended for non-payment, data is retained and access is restored when the balance is settled.

liability.title: Limits of liability
liability.p1: The service is provided with reasonable skill and care. To the extent permitted by law, our aggregate liability in any twelve-month period is limited to the fees paid for that hospital in the preceding twelve months. We are not liable for clinical outcomes or for losses caused by data the hospital entered incorrectly.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.p1: We will give notice in the workspace before a material change takes effect. Continuing to use the platform after that date constitutes acceptance.

contact.title: Contact
contact.p1: Contract and billing questions go to the platform support address, quoting the hospital subdomain. For anything urgent, call the published support number.

terms.lede: What a hospital signs up to: the trial, the billing cycle, the quotas, who owns the data and who is responsible for what.

scope.title: What this notice covers
scope.p1: This notice explains how patient and staff data moves through the SanaGo platform, who inside a hospital can see it, and what a hospital can require from us. It covers the public site you are reading and the hospital workspaces served on each hospital’s own address.

roles.title: The hospital decides, we operate
roles.p1: For clinical data the hospital is the data controller and SanaGo is the processor: the hospital decides what is collected and who may see it, and we run the system on its behalf. For account and billing data on the platform console, we act as controller.

isolation.title: One hospital, one database
isolation.p1: Every hospital is provisioned with its own database and its own subdomain. There is no shared table holding several hospitals’ patients. A session opened on one hospital’s address cannot read another hospital’s records, even with a valid login.

access.title: Who can see a record
access.b1: Access is granted per role and per action, not per person and not by sharing a login.
access.b2: A doctor sees the patients they treat and the results attached to them; a cashier sees billing lines, not clinical notes.
access.b3: Sensitive actions — dispensing, discharge, refunds, exports — are recorded against the user who performed them.
access.b4: Platform staff cannot browse clinical records. Support access happens through a hospital-created account or an explicit, logged impersonation by the platform administrator.

audit.title: The audit trail
audit.p1: Privileged actions on the platform are written to an audit log with the actor, the hospital concerned, the origin address and the payload. A hospital administrator can read the trail for their own hospital; the platform administrator reads platform-level events.

processors.title: Third parties involved
processors.b1: Transactional email for account, notification and support messages.
processors.b2: SMS delivery over mobile networks for appointment and result notices, when the hospital enables it.
processors.b3: The hosting and database infrastructure that stores the hospital’s data, with access limited to platform operators and covered by our agreements with them.

retention.title: Retention and export
retention.p1: Records are retained for as long as the hospital’s subscription is active. A hospital can request a full export of its data at any time and, when it leaves, receive a final export before its database is decommissioned.
retention.p2: Operational logs are kept for a shorter window, sized for support and security review rather than long-term archival.

rights.title: Requests from patients and staff
rights.p1: Patients and hospital staff direct access, correction and deletion requests to the hospital that holds their record — that hospital is the controller. We support the hospital in answering them through export and correction tools in the workspace.

contact.title: Contact
contact.p1: Questions about this notice, a data-handling agreement or an export request go to the platform support address below. If you are a patient, contact the hospital that holds your record first.

privacy.lede: A short, specific notice — written for the hospital director who has to sign a data-handling agreement, and the administrator who has to answer a patient.
